description.value: A functional MRI study of healthy premenopausal women examining how experimentally manipulated social support affects brain activation, effective connectivity during food-cue processing, and overeating-related behavior.

spans.text: This study used functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and dynamic causal modeling (DCM) analysis to elucidate the general neural mechanisms and effective neural pathways linking social support to alterations in food cue processing and overeating.

description.value: Two-session randomized parallel-group study. Participants were assigned to social support or non-social support groups in Session 1, completed behavioral assessments, underwent social support and stress manipulations, performed the Food Incentive Delay task during fMRI in Session 2, and completed food choice and bogus tasting measures afterward.

Food Incentive Delay (FID) task

description.value: A modified Food Incentive Delay task in which geometric cues signaled high-calorie food, low-calorie food, or a pixelated control outcome, followed by anticipation, an arrow-direction response, and feedback.

spans.text: During each trial, participants were first presented with a geometric figure (cue), followed by a fixed interval (anticipation), and then responded to the direction of an arrow with a button press (reaction).
Participants were informed that they could win high-calorie foods (e.g., chips), low-calorie foods (e.g., cherry tomatoes), or nothing (pixelated control) based on their reaction performance.

description.value: Measures cognitive restraint, uncontrolled eating, and emotional eating.

spans.text: The Three-Factor Eating Questionnaire (TFEQ-R18) is a scale that measures three domains of eating behavior: cognitive restraint (e.g., “I deliberately take small helpings to control my weight”), uncontrolled eating (e.g., “Sometimes when I start eating, I just can't seem to stop”) and emotional eating (e.g., “I start to eat when I feel anxious”) ( Karlsson et al., 2000 ).
